notes: The Laboratory/Experiments subsystem lives in engine/experiments.py: the setup terminal, pause/resume, the generic cap and day_gate machinery, and effect application. Records carrying 'implemented': true are live; the rest are inert and carry meta.blocked_on naming what each still needs. Live triggers fire from engine/experiments.py (immediately), Game._place_room via on_room_drafted (the five draft-site triggers), special_items.open_container (trunks_opened) and two sites in game.py (security_door). See docs/experiments-design.md for the phase plan and its Status section for the current live counts -- that section, not this note, is the one kept in step with each PR.

Deliberately never modelled, at any future phase (see docs/experiments-design.md): the 40-second real-time trigger and the map-view trigger (no wall-clock or interactive map action in this simulator); the setup-menu reroll timing exploit (revisiting the Experimental Setup menu before committing to reroll the three-of-each draw -- a UI-timing exploit, not a data rule); radiation level (a hidden daily counter, incremented by every successful trigger, that gates the Shelter terminal's unlock-all-doors ability -- Shelter/radiation are out of scope); Dare Mode (an alternate, harder experiments ruleset documented on a separate wiki subpage); Research Logs (an in-fiction in-game log of experiment activation history, not a mechanical system).

mechanic.setup: Three experimental triggers and three experimental effects are chosen uniformly from the available pool at the Laboratory terminal; the player picks one of each to form the day's experiment.
mechanic.packet_note: The Satellite Dish data packet permanently adds the 8 packet triggers and 8 packet effects to the pool, bringing each to 20; Packet Management then lets the player choose which >=8 of each may appear. Phases 5-8 (out of scope for this data pass).

triggers.text: Immediately,

notes: Triggers exactly once, at the moment the experiment is started.

triggers.text: Each time you eat an apple,

notes: Counts green apples and apples-with-leaves consumed for steps; no other fruit counts. The steps from the apple are gained before the experimental effect applies. Our single apple dish id covers all three visual varieties (purely visual per the wiki), so every apple eaten fires this trigger once, from special_items.eat_food after the steps grant.

triggers.text: Whenever you draft a Shop room,

notes: All Shops count. Can loop with the Aquariums effect. With Blessing of the Tinkerer active, drafting the Electric Eel Aquarium triggers this twice (most triggers do not double this way): effects/rooms/shrine.py fires trigger_success on every Mechanical Room draft while the blessing holds, and the Aquarium chain then fires this record on its own terms.

triggers.text: Each time you unlock or bypass a security door,

availability.text: If Veteran Mode is not enabled, this trigger cannot appear before Day 8.

notes: A security door must be drafted FROM to count; merely unlocking one is not enough.
"Opening a security door in a different room by drafting into it also counts for this experimental trigger."

Wiki also hedges that this 'occasionally triggers an additional time at the start of the draft, possibly due to a bug,' with no rate given; magnitude.undocumented_extra_fire_rate_pct left null (gap -- do not invent) and deliberately not modelled.

triggers.text: Whenever you spend 2 or more gems drafting a room,

notes: Applies to whichever rooms currently cost >=2 gems to draft -- the wiki page resolves this via a live Cargo query (Gem_cost>=2 AND NOT Type HOLDS 'Upgrade'), not a static id list, so no room id list is transcribed here. Waived if a room's gem cost is removed (e.g. by the Emerald Bracelet); gems spent elsewhere during drafting (e.g. the Study's option) do not count.

triggers.text: For each Bedroom you draft after your second,

notes: Wiki: "The first two Bedrooms drafted do not count for this trigger, but each Bedroom drafted afterwards does. It does matter whether those two initial Bedrooms are drafted before or after starting the experiment." That last sentence never says which way it matters and the wiki gives no further detail -- it has never been grammatically clean. Owner ruling: this sim counts all of today's Bedrooms toward the two-Bedroom threshold, whether drafted before or after the experiment started.
The Bunk Room counts twice, and can by itself satisfy both of the 'first two' -- if drafted with exactly one other Bedroom already in the house, the experiment triggers once.

triggers.text: Whenever you draft an 'archived' floorplan,

availability.text: If Veteran Mode is not enabled, this trigger cannot appear until you have drafted an Archives at least once.

notes: Requires first drafting the Archives (whose effect hides floorplans during drafting) and then drafting one of the hidden ones. An archived Bunk Room triggers twice.

triggers.text: The next 3 times you unlock and open a chest,

notes: 'Chest' is wiki terminology for trunk; counts both key-unlocks and Sledge-Hammer-equivalent smashes. Fires for containers.kinds 'trunk' and the dead 'chest' kind (no room currently references it); does not fire for lockers, the Garage car trunk, or Vault deposit boxes, which are distinct mechanics.

triggers.text: When you draft a Hallway from another Hallway,

notes: Counts Hallways of all kinds, not just the base Hallway room.

triggers.text: Each time you find some trash while digging,

availability.text: If Veteran Mode is not enabled, this trigger cannot appear until the first time you obtain a Shovel.

notes: Six wiki-listed trash kinds (rock, pebbles, tin can, brick, shoe, nail) plus Scraps of Paper (Patch 1.6+). Digging up 'nothing' does not count. Fires from special_items.dig_all's per-spot loop on a 'junk' table outcome; both dig tables already fold Scraps of Paper into a second junk row, so no separate handling is needed for the Patch 1.6 addition. The item_obtained_gate availability (first Shovel obtained) is not enforced -- only day_gate is -- so this trigger is always offerable; veteran_mode (default True) would bypass the gate anyway.

triggers.text: When you draft a Red Room, lose 5 steps and then,

notes: One of the few triggers that carries its own baked-in effect (the 5-step loss, floored at 0) on top of whichever effect is chosen for the column. The step loss can be nullified by pairing with the 'set steps to 40' effect.

triggers.text: While drafting, if you draw a DRAWING ROOM floorplan,

availability.text: If Veteran Mode is not enabled, this trigger cannot appear before Day 8.

notes: Triggers on every draw of the Drawing Room including redraws, and even when rewinding back into a previous draw with the Chronograph.

triggers.text: The first time you enter each room on Rank 9,

notes: Includes the Antechamber. Prior visits before the experiment started do not count.

triggers.text: For each room with a fireplace you draft,

notes: The Dining Room only counts when drafted in the center of the house or on Rank 9; on the wings or Rank 1 its fireplace wall is windows instead.

triggers.text: For every room you draft within the next 40 seconds,

meta.blocked_on: permanent: this simulator has no wall clock, so a real-time trigger has no meaning here
notes: Real-time based (~7 triggers achievable at high speed); deliberately never modelled -- this simulator has no wall-clock concept, so the trigger is meaningless here regardless of implementation phase.

triggers.text: Each time you access a different terminal today,

notes: First access per terminal since the experiment started, including via Remote Terminal Access.

triggers.text: Each time you draft an upgraded floorplan,

notes: Multiple copies of the same upgraded floorplan each trigger separately; an upgraded Bunk Room triggers twice.

triggers.text: Each time you pull a different antechamber lever,

notes: Only unique levers pulled after the experiment started count; levers pulled beforehand never (re)trigger it.

triggers.text: The next 10 times you view your map, lose 10 steps and then,

availability.text: If this trigger is offered today, the "set your steps to 40" effect has a 95% chance to be removed from today's effect pool.

meta.blocked_on: permanent: this simulator has no interactive map-viewing action to trigger on
notes: Deliberately never modelled -- there is no interactive map-viewing action in this simulator, so the trigger is meaningless here regardless of implementation phase.

triggers.text: Each time you draft a Tomorrow room,

notes: 'Tomorrow Rooms' are the 12 records carrying extra_categories: ["tomorrow"] in rooms.json (break_room__ix11, sauna, coat_check, mail_room, mail_room__ix89/90/91, freezer, hallway__ix76, morning_room, clock_tower, planetarium) -- the same category Game.end_day already reads for the Clock Tower's own next-day key pulse.

effects.text: gain 1 key, 1 gem or 1 die (selected randomly)

notes: The key/gem/die selection split is not published by the wiki; magnitude.split is inferred as a uniform one-third-each roll, not sourced -- revisit if a source ever settles the real weights.
Originally granted a coin instead of the die; the coin reward was replaced with an Ivory Die in Patch 1.04.5 (provenance only, not current behavior).

effects.text: set your Steps to 40.

notes: Nullifies the Red Rooms trigger's own steps penalty. If triggered by drafting the Weight Room, steps are set to 40 THEN halved to 20 by the Weight Room's own effect.

effects.text: add a small chest to the Entrance Hall.

notes: 17 is a hard, wiki-stated cap (predetermined spawn order across the Entrance Hall's four walls). Shared with The Twins constellation, whose effect is identical to triggering this effect twice -- so the counter this effect bumps (special.entrance_hall_trunks) is named for the Entrance Hall, not for this experiment record, and is reusable once The Twins is modelled.

Owner ruling, from play: the 17 cap and the trunks it spawns are a DAILY maximum -- neither carries over to the next day. No GameConfig field or carryover() entry; SpecialItemsState is rebuilt fresh with GameState every day, which already gives this the right reset semantics for free.
"There is no difference between a 'small chest' and a regular trunk" (wiki): modelled by reusing the existing containers.kinds 'trunk' entry rather than inventing a distinct 'small_chest' kind.

Wiki: the effect "will no longer have any effect" past the cap, distinct from mail_room_letter's "never offered again" -- this effect stays offerable forever, it just silently no-ops once 17 trunks have been added.

effects.text: gain 1 key for every 2 Hallways in your house.

notes: If the Hallway trigger itself drafted the counted Hallway, that Hallway is included in the count.

effects.text: gain +1 star.

availability.text: This effect will only appear if you have at least 3 stars, are on Veteran Mode, or have set up an experiment packet.

effects.text: gain 3 gold for each red room in your house.

notes: Triggers successfully with no effect if there are currently no Red Rooms in the estate.

effects.text: spread dirt on the driveway.

availability.text: This effect will never be offered if the "find trash while digging" experiment trigger is offered.

meta.blocked_on: Grounds branch unimplemented: off-grid dig spots have no representation in this simulator (special_items.dig_all reads state.grid[cell] only; engine/areas.py has no dig-spot concept) -- only this record's Conference Room branch is implemented.
notes: The 2/3/4 dig-spot-per-trigger distribution is not published by the wiki; magnitude.distribution left null (gap -- do not invent). engine/experiments.py::_apply_spread_dig_spots always adds 3 (the wiki's stated usual batch) rather than inventing a roll across the three options.

Wiki gives only approximate totals for the Grounds branch, not exact caps: 'approximately 100 dig spots... after around 34 experiment triggers' -- unbuilt (see meta.blocked_on), so no cap field recorded for it, unlike the exact 17/16/40/3/10 caps on other records.

The Conference Room branch's cap IS exact and published ("up to 50 dig spots... after 17 triggers"): recorded as magnitude.conference_room_spot_cap (50) rather than the top-level cap field, because cap counts successful APPLICATIONS (see ExperimentEffect's own field comment) while this branch's limit is a spot TOTAL -- 17 triggers of 3 spots each is 51, one more than the stated 50, so the engine enforces the spot cap directly (clamping the final batch) rather than an application count that would occasionally overshoot by one spot.

"The first five [dig spots] appearing on the conference table and the remainder appearing on the surrounding floor" (wiki) is placement flavour with no mechanical consequence at this engine's per-cell granularity; not modelled.

KNOWN GAP, not built: the Dovecote birdbath sub-effect. Wiki: with a Dovecote on the estate, this effect ALSO fills 6 off-grid birdbaths with dirt in a fixed 3-trigger pattern (3 birdbaths on the first trigger, 2 on the second, 1 on the third), 'entirely independent of the main effect' and occurring 'regardless of whether the regular dig spots are spread to the Grounds or the Conference Room.' Off-grid like the Grounds branch itself, so blocked on the same missing off-grid dig-spot concept.

KNOWN GAP, not built: the Blessing of the Chef 'Mudslide Icecream' dish. Wiki: while that Blessing is active, triggering this effect can add a unique Dining Room dish (5 steps, plus a dirt-pile flavour detail) -- the Blessing system itself is unimplemented, so this is out of scope until that lands.

effects.text: set your dice to 2.

notes: UNPUBLISHED, DO NOT IMPLEMENT AS AN AVAILABILITY RULE: the wiki source carries this rule commented out (not live text): 'This effect cannot be offered if the gain 1 key/gem/die effect is offered.' The editors have not confirmed it and flag the broader datamine as unreliable ('a lot of the datamined info on experiments has been off or just straight up wrong'). Recorded here for provenance only -- the effect's own mechanics (set dice to 2) are unaffected and are implemented.

effects.text: add 3 Aquariums to today's draft pool.

notes: The rarity_override and priority_draw_chance_pct fields are wiki-datamined (tagged DataSpoiler) rather than plain wiki text, unlike the '3 Aquariums' headline number.
Added Aquariums have different placement restrictions than the original Aquarium, which can make the count look smaller than it is.

effects.text: a letter will be delivered to the Mail Room.

availability.text: This effect cannot appear until Day 11, unless a custom experiment packet has been created.

notes: 16 letters total, delivered in a fixed predetermined order regardless of whether the Mail Room is on the estate; never offered again once all 16 are delivered (the wiki-stated cap).

Owner ruling: the 16 letters are pure flavour (safe codes, a network password, a puzzle solution, which rooms carry steam ducts) -- none grants a resource, item, or unlock, and the assumed-solved doctrine already grants everything they convey (same reasoning as the Speakeasy: docs/doctrine.md, 'Puzzles are assumed solved'). Letter contents are deliberately unmodelled; the effect is a plain delivered-count bump.

The 'never offered again' cap counts deliveries across the whole save: ExperimentState.letters_delivered is seeded from GameConfig.letters_delivered at reset, reported by carryover(), carried by DayChain, and deliberately absent from the attempt wrap -- the same shape as GameConfig.chapel_tithes. The 16 letters' own contents are deliberately unmodelled (owner ruling: they are flavour, and the assumed-solved doctrine already grants what they convey).

effects.text: permanently add 1 gold to your allowance.
lose 10 steps and gain 20 gold.
stock your PANTRY with fruit.

availability.text: This effect can only appear if there is a Pantry already in the estate when first viewing experiment options.

meta.blocked_on: permanent for now: no Pantry-stocking mechanic exists to add fruit to
notes: The exact fruit mix (apple vs banana vs orange weights) is not published, only their relative ordering (apples less common than bananas and oranges); magnitude.mix_weights left null (gap -- do not invent).

This ordering is specific to the experiment-spawned Pantry fruit pool, not the general fruit pool: items.json's fruit_weights has apples MORE common than bananas/oranges (50/30/20) for ordinary spawns. The two are different pools describing different situations, not a contradiction -- do not 'reconcile' them.

effects.text: Lower the Reservoir by 1

availability.text: If the Reservoir's water level is 0 when this experimental effect is randomly chosen during setup, it is changed to 'Raise the Reservoir by 1' (identical mechanism, reversed direction, water_delta effectively +1). Once either variant is rolled during setup it is locked in for the rest of the day even if the water level changes again before the experiment begins.

meta.blocked_on: no reservoir ROOM exists -- the Reservoir is an areas.json node only, so there is nothing on the grid whose water level an effect could raise or lower

effects.text: remove a crate from the tunnel.

meta.blocked_on: the Crate Tunnel is owner-ruled out of scope, so there are no crates to remove
notes: UNPUBLISHED, DO NOT IMPLEMENT: the wiki source carries this rule commented out (not live text): 'If fewer than 36 crates... have been removed, this effect has a 30% chance to be removed from today's effect pool,' with the editor's own note that they tested it and found no meaningful frequency change, and a general caution that a lot of the datamined experiments info 'has been off or just straight up wrong.' Recorded here for provenance only.

Actual crate removal is gated on the tunnel's left torch being lit (engine/special_items.py ignition targets do not currently include the tunnel); the trigger message still displays and the count still advances even when unlit, with removal applied retroactively once lit.

effects.text: unseal one of the doors of the ANTECHAMBER.

notes: The wiki states west/east/south doors 'appear to be preferred' over north but gives no numbers; magnitude.weighting left null (gap -- do not invent).
Has no effect once all four doors are unsealed (still triggers, no-op).

Mechanically implemented (engine/experiments.py::_apply_unseal_antechamber_door), but pool="packet" keeps it undrawable in setup until the packet subsystem itself (phases 5-8) is authorised -- see the packet_note in this file's mechanic block. Unseals the first still-sealed segment in west/south/east/north order (the same order Game.__init__ seals them in), reusing Game._open_segment -- the same low-level call every Antechamber lever room already makes -- rather than a weighted pick, since magnitude.weighting is unpublished.

effects.text: gain 1 key for every 30 steps you have.

notes: Mechanically implemented (engine/experiments.py), but pool="packet" keeps it undrawable in setup until the packet subsystem itself (phases 5-8) is authorised -- see the packet_note in this file's mechanic block.

effects.text: permanently increase your lockpicking skill.

meta.blocked_on: no lockpicking-skill stat exists to raise, and the wiki does not publish its magnitude either (magnitude.amount stays null)
notes: The magnitude of the skill increase is not published anywhere -- the wiki notes there is no in-game way to check lockpicking skill at all short of tallying Research Log activation counts; magnitude.amount left null (gap -- do not invent).
The Pick Sound Amplifier also benefits from this skill (wiki-confirmed).

effects.text: gain 1 random item, then set your keys to 0.

notes: The eligible item pool is a live wiki Cargo query (Items where Locations HOLDS 'Experiment'), not present in static wikitext; magnitude.item_pool left null (gap -- do not invent). If fewer than 2 pool items are currently available to spawn, a Silver Key is granted instead.

Mechanically implemented (engine/experiments.py::_apply_random_item_then_zero_keys), but pool="packet" keeps it undrawable in setup until the packet subsystem itself (phases 5-8) is authorised -- see the packet_note in this file's mechanic block. Since the true item pool is unpublished (above), the random item is instead drawn from the same generic extra-item table (items.EXTRA_ITEM_TABLE: coins/key/gem/die) Closet/Walk-In/Attic and gain_key_gem_or_die already use, rather than inventing a special-item list; the wiki's fewer-than-2-available Silver Key fallback is not modelled since that table is a fixed 4 entries and never that small.

effects.text: lose half your steps, then gain 4 Ivory Die.

notes: Mechanically implemented (engine/experiments.py::_apply_half_steps_for_dice), but pool="packet" keeps it undrawable in setup until the packet subsystem itself (phases 5-8) is authorised -- see the packet_note in this file's mechanic block. Steps are floored (math.floor(steps * 0.5), so an odd count like 7 becomes 3, not 4) and lost before the 4 Ivory Die are granted, per the wiki's stated order; the dice are still granted even when the step loss alone ends the day (see the function's own docstring for why no termination check is added here).
